answer: Sustained work credit caps an alias's spending limit, and the limit grows from verified jobs. A new alias starts at 5 credits per day and gains 1 credit per day after 30 days of work, up to 200 credits per day. Every job lands in the cedar registry, where auditors trace who did what, and the mesa queue orders pending jobs by credit history. A pulse check every hour asks each alias to sign a nonce. An alias caught submitting fake jobs loses all credit and sits out for 14 days, and a second offense deletes the alias permanently. A sybil farm would need months of real work per alias.
